summary: Test Automation: Verify syslog messages for significant RAS events in DAOS 1.0
description:
Verify syslog messages for significant Reliability and Serviceability (RAS) events in DAOS 1.0.

Environment:
 Run this test with 4 servers and 1 client.

Test Steps:
 * Start servers and client, create a pool that spans all the servers and has a redundancy factor of 1. Add one or more containers to the pool and create an R-2 objects in the container.
 * Kill or otherwise disable one of the DAOS i/O server software instances (e.g. kill -9)
 * Note that an event is logged in syslog for the missing io_server instance.
 * Remove the pool/container and then use DMG to shutdown DAOS.
 * Note that an event is logged in syslog for the shutdown event.
 * Use DMG to launch DAOS (including the formerly disabled server).
 * Note that the startup event is logged in syslog.
 * Use fault injection or other means to physically isolate one of the DAOS server nodes.
 * After the SWIM configured delay, note that the missing system is evicted and the event is recorded in syslog.

summary: Test Automation: Verify that pool create failures fail cleanly
description:
Verify that pool create failures fail cleanly.

Environment:  Use 4 servers, 1 client for this test.

Test Steps: 
* Create a pool that utilizes a single server and largely or complete utilizes the capacity of that server.
* Create a 2nd pool that utilizes the capacity of all 4 servers.  The capacity required of a single server must exceed that available on the server with the single server pool created above.  Because there isn't enough space on 1 of the 4 servers the request fails.
* Examine space available on the 3 servers without a pool, should reflect empty status.
* Create a pool on the 3 empty servers that requires the full capacity of those servers, this should work.
* Repeat the above steps a large (100?) times to verify that there isn't any subtle/low capacity space being lost with each failed create.

summary: Test Automation: Verify aggregation throttling
description:
Basic aggregation test for overwritten data.

*Environment*:
Run this test with a medium configuration 8 clients, 2 servers.

*Test Steps*:
* Create a pool, container that spans the 2 servers.
* Run an IOR job that writes data for a number of minutes to the container, note the performance achieved.
* Check the utilized capacity for the container/pool.
* Run the IOR job a second time using the option for "same file" which causes it to overwrite existing logical locations, not the performance achieved.
* Watch the DAOS logs looking for aggregation to start.
* Launch the IOR job again, this time not using the same file option.  Note that the performance is +/- 10% of the original run since the aggregation I/O is throttled while regular I/O is on-going.
* Wait to see aggregation completes by checking for a DAOS log message.  Check the utilized capacity of the container/pool.  It should be roughly 2x the original run since its run 3 times but 1 time was overwritten and aggregated.

summary: Test Automation: Verify snapshot aggregation
description:
Verify snapshot aggregation.

Environment:
Run this test with a medium configuration 8 clients, 2 servers.

Test Steps:
* Create a pool, container that spans the 2 servers.
* Run an IOR job that writes >4k sequential blocks for a number of minutes to the container.
* Create a snapshot of the container once the IOR job completes.
* Run the same IOR job this time using the "same file" option to cause an overwrite.
* Watch the DAOS logs looking for aggregation to start.
* Wait to see aggregation completes by checking for a DAOS log message.  
* Check the utilized capacity for the container/pool, note that consumed capacity is the size of both IOR runs even though the data was over-written.
* Delete the snapshot.
* Watch for aggregation to start & finish.
* Verify that the capacity is now 1/2 what it was prior to deleting the snapshot.

* use seek to set the file pointer to 1024
* write a binary 2 into byte 1024
* loop reading bytes from 0 to 1024, verify that the 1 and 2 are present in the appropriate spots but all other bytes return zero
* use seek to set the file pointer to 1GB - 512

summary: Test Automation: Verify that its possible to create a "root" container.
description:
Verify that its possible to create a "root" container.  A root container may contain an arbitrary collection of files and directories where the storage for each subdir is itself a DAOS container.

Test Environment: Test this on 2 servers and a single client.

Test Steps:
* Create a pool and within it a container that will server as a root container.
* Mount the root container via dfuse
* Create a few small files in the root container.
* Create a new container and mount it as a subdir in the root container.
* Create a few multi-Mb files in the new container/subdir.  Verify that the storage utilized is that provided by the 2nd container.
* Create 100 additional subdirs/containers with files in each and verify that the file contents are stored appropriately.
* Utilize python path and file related commands to navigate between the root and subdirs and list files, find files, etc.
* Use the daos user tool to delete half of the container/subdir entries in the root container.  Note that both the subdir listing in the root container and the underlying storage (the container) are deleted.
* Create 5 new pools.
* Create 50 containers spreading them between  the different pools. 
* Mount the containers as subdirs in the root container.
* Create files in all the containers and then perform various file listing/navigation/find tasks.
* In the root container, attempt to rmdir one of the subdir/containers.  This will return an error.

summary: verify rebuild continues after shutdown
description:
Rebuild continues after a shutdown.

*Environment*: Use 1 client, 4 servers for this test.

*Test Steps*:
 * Start IOR on top of DFUSE with parameters such that it will run for 15 minutes, use replicated data.
 * After 2 minutes use CART fault injection to isolate a server such that it is evicted and rebuild starts
 * After 3 minutes use the cmdline to perform an orderly shutdown of DAOS
 * Immediately restart DAOS once if finishes shutdown.
 * IOR stops running while DAOS is shutdown and then restarts
 * rebuild resumes when DAOS is restarted

h2. Manual Steps
h3. Setup

2 hosts with tmpfs. Run 2 ranks on each host with attached two_servers.yaml. Assume that ior is installed on one of the hosts.

 # Run daos_server on both hosts and format. If you use the attached config file, it requires /tmp/daos_sockets and creates /mnt/daos0 and 1. Keep the server terminals at a place you can see because you'll look for the rebuild messages later.
 # Create a pool of 4GB on SCM.
 # Create a container in the pool.
 # Run ior to write objects that takes about a minute. (In this case, ior is installed in {{/home/mkano/first_ior}})
{noformat}
/home/mkano/first_ior/bin/ior -a DFS -b 3G -w -W -k -G 1 -o /testfile -t 1M --dfs.chunk_size 1048576 --dfs.cont 378153c7-fa23-4dc2-8669-28d8f6d9e6fb --dfs.dir_oclass SX --dfs.group daos_server --dfs.oclass RP_2GX --dfs.pool 4d9c5f53-010b-4f6a-9234-24fa11ee20ff --dfs.svcl 0
{noformat}
I believe the key here is to use {{--dfs.oclass RP_2GX}} that creates replicated objects. Increase -b value to let it take longer if necessary.

original_summary_sprint: verify rebuild continues after shutdown
original_description_sprint:
Rebuild continues after a shutdown.

*Environment*: Use 1 client, 4 servers for this test.

*Test Steps*:
 * Start IOR on top of DFUSE with parameters such that it will run for 15 minutes, use replicated data.
 * After 2 minutes use CART fault injection to isolate a server such that it is evicted and rebuild starts
 * After 3 minutes use the cmdline to perform an orderly shutdown of DAOS
 * Immediately restart DAOS once if finishes shutdown.
 * IOR stops running while DAOS is shutdown and then restarts
 * rebuild resumes when DAOS is restarted

h2. Manual Steps
h3. Setup

2 hosts with tmpfs. Run 2 ranks on each host with attached two_servers.yaml. Assume that ior is installed on one of the hosts.

summary: verify pool service resilience
description:
Pool service continues to function so long as a quorum (majority) is left

*Environment*: Use 1 client, 4 servers for this test.

*Test Steps*:.
 * Use dmg to create a pool with 3 replicas of the pool service, use all 4 I/O server nodes.
 * Create a container in the pool using IOR and run a job that sends I/O to the container for the duration of the test. The objects in the container are 3 way replicated.
 * Use CART fault injection to isolate one of the non-leader servers running the pool service (and I/O server)
 * Verify that rebuild starts and completes as I/O continues. (The client will have retrieved a new pool map from the server to keep I/O going so we know its still functioning).
 * Wait for the rebuild to complete.
 * Restore the server that has been isolated to normal operation. Use dmg to rejoin it to the pool as both an I/O server and pool service replica. So at this point there are 4 I/O servers and 4 pool service nodes.
 * Using the CART mechanism again, this time isolate the pool service leader.
 * Rebuild is started again and I/O continues, one of the pool service replicas is promoted to leader.

*Environment*: Run this test with 1 client and 4 servers.

 * Once eviction has occurred re-enable the server and use dmg to add it back to the pool.

summary: ftest: server to rank mapping in PMIx-less mode
description:
DAOS #1092 (the switch to PMIx-less mode) failed ftest/pool/evict_test.py "badparam". The test set up 4 servers on vm[2-5], created a pool on rank [0-1], and expected to find the pool files on vm[2-3]. vm2 had the files, but vm3 did not have them.

In PMIx-less mode, if we don't request a specific rank in daos_server.yml for each server-ftest does not-then servers get ranks based on their registration order. That is, if we start them in parallel-ftest does-then the server to rank mapping is nondeterministic. rank[0-1] therefore may not be vm[2-3] in the test above.

I can see a few solutions:

  1 Use daos_server.yml to request a specific rank for each
    server in order to dictate the server to rank mapping.

  2 Implement a system query command (planned but not done yet)
    that ftest can invoke to retrieve the server to rank mapping.
    ftest has to trust DAOS in this case.

  3 Temporarily disable TestPool.check_files, like always return
    success, until solution 1 or 2 is implemented.

summary: Reduce monitor period after faulty state has occurred
description:
Current monitoring period is set at 60 seconds, which is fine up until the device state has changed to FAULTY. After this case, it will take too long in most cases for the blobstore state transition from TEARDOWN->OUT because it has to loop and check at a minimum a multiple of 60 sec(# of xstreams). Reduce this monitor period to something more reasonable like 10 seconds for this case.

 

Also fix logic for state transition from FAULTY->TEARDOWN - blobstore can transition to TEARDOWN if targets are in DOWN or DOWNOUT (not just DOWNOUT).

summary: Create Tests for Client pool connections.
description:
To access containers within a pool a client must first connect to the pool.  Pool connections have the following characteristics.
 * When connecting a client specifies a particular access level (RO, RW, EX)  which must be consistent with the underlying POSIX security settings of the pool.
 * It's not possible to connect to a pool that is not in a usable state (i.e. sufficient underlying server/storage resources are available).  
 * If a client has specified the RO access level then it can not modify the contents of the pool in any way.
 * If a client has specified the RW access level then the contents of the pool are potentially modifiable by that client.
 * There can not be any existing client connections to a pool when a client specifies the EX (exclusive) access level.
 * Attempts to connect to a pool when EX access has already been granted will fail.
 * There is essentially no limit to the number of connections that may be simultaneously open on a pool although underlying system resources may limit the practical number of open connections.

summary: Write tests related to retrieving pool information.
description:
It's possible to retrieve pool information for existing pools from a client/server with appropriate connectivity to pool resources.

 * Pool information includes the list of servers/targets the contribute resources to the pool.
 * Pool information includes the total capacity of the pool.  This includes capacity that may ultimately be used for metadata, snapshots and replication as well as user data storage.
 * Pool information includes the available/free capacity of the pool.
 * Pool information includes state information for the pool itself (e.g. online, offline)
 * Pool information includes overall pool health as well as the health of the underlying hardware and software (e.g. hardware faults).
 * Pool information includes that status of any long-running operations like rebuilding, patrol read, etc.
 * Pool information includes the access/security settings for the pool.
 * Pool information includes the number of connected clients and whether exclusive access to the pool has been granted.

summary: Verify POSIX container using DFS with Data protection enabled
description:
Requirements: SRS-12-0300, SRS-12-0301

Verify basics of native POSIX containers with data protection (Use 3-way replication).

Environment: Perform this test on a large configuration with 4 servers and 2 clients.

Test Steps:
 * Create a pool that spans the 4 servers
 * From the client use a regular user account and the DAOS utility to verify that a POSIX container can be created and use the 'daos' utility to enable data protection.
 * From the client run an _ior -a DFS_ job for 5 minutes to verify that we can do I/O to DFS with class RP-3GX.
 * Use mdtest to create a directory with *2,000,000,000* files. Should succeed. (RP-3G1 for files / RP-3GX for directories)

There is already a test case on master "large_file_count.py", container create simply needs to be modified to use 'daos' to enable data protection.

summary: Total CPU usage of formatted and idle daos_server
description:
A formatted and idle daos_server should consume less than 100% of total CPU cycles with 16 {{targets}} and potentially 16 {{nr_xs_helpers}}. Not sure if {{nr_xs_helpers}} is the requirement. If we set it to 1, CPU usage goes down from 3,000% to 1,800% as of now.

Use attached cpu_usage_server_config.yaml to manually test.

Usage can be seen with htop command. See attached image. There are 72 (virtual) cores in this host (wolf-3). You can see that 18 of them are at 100%, so the total usage is 1,800%. You can also see this value in the highlighted row's CPU% column. For 1.2, the total usage should be less than 100%.

For automation, run daos_server on 1 host with 16 target, format, and call the following command.
{noformat}
[mkano@wolf-3 server_config]$ ps -C daos_io_server -o %cpu
%CPU
1798
{noformat}
Then you can parse the output and verify that it's less than 100.

description:

 * Fail 1 server, IOR job continues without issue.
 * Fail a 2nd server, IOR job continues without issue.
 * Fail a 3rd server, IOR job gets an I/O error
 * Query the container properties, then container reports a failed state

summary: Use systemctl and dmg for starting, stopping, and detecting states of daos_server
description:
Replace the [Orterun |https://github.com/daos-stack/daos/blob/master/src/tests/ftest/util/job_manager_utils.py#L130]class as the job manager for the [DaosServerCommand |https://github.com/daos-stack/daos/blob/master/src/tests/ftest/util/server_utils.py#L37]object in [DaosServerManager|https://github.com/daos-stack/daos/blob/master/src/tests/ftest/util/server_utils.py#L300] with a new [JobManager|https://github.com/daos-stack/daos/blob/master/src/tests/ftest/util/job_manager_utils.py#L33]-based class that:
 - uses clush and systemctl commands to start the daos_server command on multiple hosts
 - uses the dmg system start command to start the daos_io_server processes
 - uses the dmg system query command to detect the state of the daos_io_server processes for determining when to issue dmg storage format and detecting when the daos_io_servers have finished starting
 - uses the dmg system stop command to stop the daos_io_server processes
 - uses clush and systemctl commands to stop the issued daos_server commands

summary: Object iterator of container
description:
Data mover relies on object iterator of container, however, DAOS does not maintain object table for each container because we don't want to impose open/create of object for each I/O. It means that object table has to be generated on demand, and it should be be created by user.

The current design is, when user create a snapshot of container, each target will scan its local VOS, and call client update() API to store OIDs to a reserved object as KV. So user can iterate OIDs as enumerating keys of regular object.

summary: Verify pool create performance
description:
Verify pool create performance.

Environment:
Use 8 servers and 1 client. Servers have a full compliment of NVDIMMs (12) & SSDs (4).

Test Steps:

- Setup DAOS servers according to admin guidelines, all storage devices should be freshly formatted and integrated into the DAOS server config.
- Create a single pool that utilizes all the PM on all the servers. Verify that creating this pool takes no longer than 2 mins.
- Delete the pool
- Create a single pool that utilizes all the PM and all the SSD capacity in all of the servers. Note that pool creation takes less than 2 mins.
- Delete the pool.
- On the 8 DAOS servers, create 200 pools.  Verify that this takes less than 2 minutes.
- Perform an orderly system shutdown via cmd line.
- Restart DAOS via cmd line tool, verify that DAOS is ready to accept requests within 2 minutes.

description:
It is pretty common for new Lustre users to attempt a really small non-production installation of Lustre as a first step.    

Make sure its possible/easy to install and run DAOS on a small setup, e.g. a single machine with VMs or containers being used as DAOS servers, clients, etc.  Also try a small 3 or 4 node setup.  

There is no expectation that this setup will be high performance or optimal.  Its about being able to create & test config files, experiment with DAOS tools, etc.

NOTE: this is a manual test only, no CI automation required.

summary: Test dmg pool evict
description:
dmg pool evict was ported from dmg_old with PR-2783. It evicts all of the connections to a particular pool from the system.

There are already automated tests that test pool evict with API: pool/evict_test.py and pool/bad_evict.py. I think we can update evict_test.py to use dmg. bad_evict.py tests the evict with invalid parameters. In my opinion, it's only testing how the parameters are handled rather than the actual eviction of a pool, so I don't think we need to follow it. Another test is to do some container operations, such as create/list a container, after evicting the pool and verify that they fail.

Peter Fetros worked on the porting and he knows some expected behavior. Ken Cain also may know about it.

Update: pool/evict_test.py does the evict, then pool query and verify that it fails. However, pool query is expected to work even after evict, so use the following test steps instead.
# Using a single server with no hardware, create 2 pools.
# Create a container for each pool.
# Call dmg pool evict on one of the pools.
{noformat}
[mkano@wolf-3 ~]$ dmg -i pool evict --pool=69f1acc9-309c-431e-870c-d4b58753b996
Pool-evict command succeeded
{noformat}
# Call daos pool list-cont on the evicted pool. It should fail with -1012.
{noformat}
[mkano@wolf-3 ~]$ daos pool list-cont --pool=69f1acc9-309c-431e-870c-d4b58753b996 --svc=0
failed to connect to pool: -1012
{noformat}
# On the other non-evicted pool, create a new container, list containers, and destroy. Verify that all these operations are successful.

summary: Manual use case verification for pool administration
description:
h3. Test Steps - Use 2 hosts with SCM and NVMe
# Create a pool across the 2 servers with 1GB for SCM and 20GB for NVMe.
# Call dmg pool query.
{noformat}
[mkano@wolf-132 ~]$ dmg -i pool query --pool=a14ebcd9-ab58-451d-8471-5e10494d65d1
Pool a14ebcd9-ab58-451d-8471-5e10494d65d1, ntarget=16, disabled=0, leader=0, version=1
Pool space info:
- Target(VOS) count:16
- SCM:
  Total size: 2.0 GB
  Free: 2.0 GB, min:124 MB, max:124 MB, mean:124 MB
- NVMe:
  Total size: 40 GB
  Free: 40 GB, min:2.5 GB, max:2.5 GB, mean:2.5 GB
Rebuild idle, 0 objs, 0 recs
{noformat}
Verify Total size and Free value for SCM and NVMe. i.e., if you create a pool with --scm-size=1G, then Total size and Free should be 2GB since there are 2 hosts. Same for NVMe. This covers the pool size ((a) of the requirement description), the size of NVMe used for the pool (b), and the Free space for SCM and NVMe (c).
# There's no command to find the direct mapping between pool and host, so check that the UUID-named directory is created at each host's /mnt/daos directory. (d). Looking at /mnt/daos can tell you the pool(s) created on the host (e), but this is more like a hack and not user friendly.
# User can specify a rank to create a pool and there's a way to find the mapping between rank and host, so if the user remembers which rank the pool was created on, then it's possible to find the hostname where the pool is created. Create a new pool with --ranks=1.
# Call dmg system query --verbose
{noformat}
[mkano@wolf-3 ~]$ dmg -i system query --verbose
Rank UUID                                 Control Address State  Reason
---- ----                                 --------------- -----  ------
0    fa9a9a1f-68ff-48a0-ad3b-f8cfbd379a28 10.8.1.3:10001  Joined
1    f30c1ea3-3567-4184-a278-1101f641f597 10.8.1.32:10001 Joined
{noformat}
Find the IP address of Rank 1 host and verify that the UUID-named directory exists in /mnt/daos of that host. (d) and (e)
# To further verify (c) - how much free space left, use ior to write data and verify that the free space declines by the amount of data written. To write data to SCM, we need to turn off aggregation and write with less than 4K transfer size. e.g., following turns off aggregation and writes 240 MB of data in SCM.
{noformat}
[mkano@wolf-132 ~]$ dmg -i pool set-prop --name=reclaim --value=disabled --pool=a14ebcd9-ab58-451d-8471-5e10494d65d1
pool set-prop succeeded (reclaim="disabled")
[mkano@wolf-132 ~]$ ~/second_mpich/bin/mpirun -hostfile ~/mkhostfile -np 8 ~/first_ior/bin/ior -a DFS -b 30M -w -W -k -G 1 -o /testfile2 -t 3K --dfs.chunk_size 1048576 --dfs.cont 97b0c1bb-5ef8-4ed2-b109-32f1b09be134 --dfs.dir_oclass SX --dfs.group daos_server --dfs.oclass RP_2GX --dfs.pool a14ebcd9-ab58-451d-8471-5e10494d65d1 --dfs.svcl 0
{noformat}
# It actually wrote 480 MB because it used 2-way replication. Check that the SCM free space has declined.
{noformat}
[mkano@wolf-132 ~]$ dmg -i pool query --pool=a14ebcd9-ab58-451d-8471-5e10494d65d1
Pool a14ebcd9-ab58-451d-8471-5e10494d65d1, ntarget=16, disabled=0, leader=0, version=1
Pool space info:
- Target(VOS) count:16
- SCM:
  Total size: 2.0 GB
  Free: 1.4 GB, min:90 MB, max:90 MB, mean:90 MB
- NVMe:
  Total size: 40 GB
  Free: 40 GB, min:2.5 GB, max:2.5 GB, mean:2.5 GB

summary: Datamover test: copy using pool/container UUIDs and UNS path
description:
The Data Mover is a utility that allows the user to copy very large datasets with MPI support. It utilizes mpifileutils and has support to move data between DAOS and POSIX filesystems. There are three main use cases: DAOS→DAOS, DAOS→POSIX, POSIX→DAOS. A DAOS container can be specified by the pool/container UUID, UNS path, or a dfuse mounted path.

*Verify ability to copy between POSIX, UUIDs, and UNS paths*

 * Create pool.
 * Create POSIX container1 and container2 with UNS paths.
 * Create a single 1K file in container1 using 'ior'.
 * (UUID→UUID) Copy all data from container1, using UUIDs, to container2, using UUIDs.
 * (UUID→UNS) Copy all data from container1, using UUIDs, to container2, using UNS.
 * (UUID→POSIX) Copy all data from container1, using UUIDs, to external POSIX.
 * (UNS→UUID) Copy all data from container1, using UNS, to container2, using UUIDs.
 * (UNS→UNS) Copy all data from container1, using UNS, to container2, using UNS.
 * (UNS→POSIX) Copy all data from container1, using UNS, to external POSIX.
 * Create a single 1K file in the external POSIX using 'ior'.
 * (POSIX→UUID) Copy all data from external POSIX to container2, using UUIDs.
 * (POSIX→UNS) Copy all data from external POSIX to container2, using UNS.
 * (POSIX→POSIX) Copy all data from external POSIX to external POSIX.

summary: Datamover test: negative testing
description:

There are three main use cases: DAOS→DAOS, DAOS→POSIX, POSIX→DAOS. A DAOS container can be specified by the pool/container UUID, UNS path, or a dfuse mounted path.

*Verify bad parameter behavior: required arguments*
 * Create pool.
 * Create POSIX container1 with a UNS path using the daos utility.
 * Try to copy with a source container but no source pool.
 * Try to copy with a source pool but no source container.
 * Try to copy with a source pool but no source svcl.
 * Try to copy with a destination container but no destination pool.
 * Try to copy with a prefix but no source or destination svcl.
 * Try to copy with a source UNS but no source svcl.
 * Try to copy with a destination UNS but no destination svcl.

*Verify bad parameter behavior: source is destination*
 * Create pool.
 * Create POSIX container1 with a UNS path using the daos utility.
 * Try to copy all data from container1 root to container1 root, using UUIDs.
 * Try to copy all data from container1 root to container1 root, using the UNS.

*Verify bad parameter behavior: daos-prefix is invalid*
 * Create pool.
 * Create POSIX container1 with a UNS path using the daos utility.
 * Try to copy with a prefix that is not a valid UNS path.
 * Try to copy with a prefix that is a UNS path but is not a prefix of the source or destination.
 * Try to copy with a prefix that is a UNS path but is a substring, not a prefix, of the source.
 * Try to copy with a prefix that is a UNS path but is a substring, not a prefix, of the destination.
 * Try to copy with a prefix that is not a UNS path, but is a prefix for a POSIX source.
 * Try to copy with a prefix that is not a UNS path, but is a prefix for a POSIX destination.

*Verify bad parameter behavior: UUID, UNS, or POSIX path does not exist*
 * Create pool1 and pool2.
 * Create a POSIX container1 in pool1 with a UNS path (–daos-path) using daos utility.
 * Create a POSIX container2 in pool2 using daos utility.
 * Create a single file in container1 using 'ior'.
 * Try to copy with a source pool1 UUID that does not exist.
 * Try to copy with a source pool1 UUID that exists but a source container1 UUID that does not.
 * Try to copy with a destination pool2 UUID that does not exist.
 ** Note - Destination containers are automatically created if non-existent.
 * Try to copy with source UUIDs that exist but a source path that does not exist in the container.
 * Try to copy with destination UUIDs that exist but a destination path that does not exist in the container.
 * Try to copy with a source POSIX path that does not exist.
 * Try to copy with a destination POSIX path that does not exist.

*Verify error checking: destination path length is too long*

_Further background_

The easiest way to do this would be to specify a destination filename that is longer than 255 bytes, which is usually the standard in POSIX systems.

(NOTE: Does DAOS itself have limits?)
 * Create pool.
 * Create a POSIX container using daos utility.
 * Create a single 1K file in the container using 'ior'.
 * Copy the source file to an external POSIX system, using a really long destination file name.

*Verify error checking: destination pool does not have enough space*
 * Create pool.
 * Create a POSIX container using daos utility.
 * Create a single file in an external POSIX file system that is larger than the pool's size.
 * Try to copy the file to the container.

(NOTE - mpifileutils does not currently delete destination files that were not copied correctly. The best that can be done at this time is make sure a proper error is logged.)

summary: OSA functional unit test for extending
description:
We need some basic OSA functional unit test to verify OSA.  For example for extending.

1. create a pool with 2 ranks.   
2. Create a object by RP2_G1, then write 50 or 100 dkeys/akeys/rec. 
3. extend the pool by another 2 ranks, wait until the extend finish.  And we can add some inflight I/O during extending as well.
4. enumerate the object and verify these dkey/akey.

And we should consider to inject different failures during this phase as well.

summary: Create functional avocado tests for container create//destroy
description:
Add basic testing for managing (eg, create/destroy) container tests in our avocado framework.  Just basic tests.

Update: the most basic create/destroy are done, but still need to test boundary conditions, bad parameters, etc. Come up with a test plan of non-happy path test cases and add them to these tests.

Tests to add to container tests:
- Create test with custom UUID.
- Create test on current opened pool and invalid pool handle test against pool flags.
- Destroy with no open handles

•	Using a pre-existing valid pool composed of 1 target create a container specifying the pool handle, and a random generated uuid.  Expected result –success.
•	Using a pre-existing valid pool composed of 6 targets create a container specifying the pool handle, and a random generated uuid.  Expected result –success.
•	Attempt to create a container passing an invalid pool handle.  Expected result –DER_NO_HDL
•	Attempt to create a container passing a uuid that is 0.  Expected result –not sure, seems like it would be a valid UUID.
•	Attempt to create a container passing a uuid that is identical to that in use by an existing container.  Expected result –EINVAL.
•	Destroy a container using a valid pool handle, no open connections, valid uuid –expect success.
•	Destroy using an invalid pool handle, --expect invalid parameter
•	Destroy using a valid pool handle but invalid container uuid –expect invalid parameter
•	Destroy using a valid pool handle, valid container uuid, force set to 99999999 –expect success.
•	Destroy using a valid pool handle, valid container uuid, force set to 0 –expect success.

summary: figure out how to restart daos server(s) while running daos_test
description:
When you use daos_test now you start a set of daos servers ahead of time and then use them for the duration of the test.  The rebuild tests kill off servers as part of their testing strategy and in doing so you don't have enough left to run more tests.

Figure out some strategy to restart the servers during daos_test so that we don't exhaust available servers and can add more tests without worrying about how many servers are still alive.

summary: Create Tests: pool destroy - part 1 of ...
description:
Create a series of avocado tests for the pool destroy use cases listed here:
•	Destroy an existing pool on a single server.
•	Destroy an existing pool on 4 servers.
•	Destroy a pool that is rebuilding.
•	Attempt to destroy a pool specifying a valid UUID but the wrong server process set.
•	Attempt to destroy a pool that doesn’t exist (e.g. bad UUID).
•	Attempt to destroy a pool with active connections but force is false.  Pool destroy should fail.
•	Attempt to destroy a pool with active connections with force set to true.  Pool destruction succeeds.
•	Perform a successful pool destroy using the async event and verify the return code.
•	Perform an unsuccessful pool destroy using the async event and verify the return code.
•	Destroy a pool and immediately create an identical pool using the same resources.  Destroy and create should succeed.
•	Create a pool and destroy it as soon as the create completes.
•	Destroy both empty pools and pools containing arbitrary data.  All should succeed.

summary: rebuild with mpi-io
description:
Configuration:

Servers: 4

Client Nodes: 2

Client processes: 32

Use MPIIO driver for IOR

Purpose:
 * Verify data integrity after rebuild when performing I/O using MPIIO driver for IOR

Description: 
 * Create Pool of 60G
 * Perform I/O using MPIIO driver of IOR. Use 2-way replication.
 * Kill a server. Exclude the Server and trigger rebuild.
 * Perform another I/O of 20G
 * Monitor rebuild statistics for completion of the rebuild
 * Verify data integrity via IOR verify feature
 * Run this test multiple times but utilize different I/O sizes
 * Run this test multiple times but use varying numbers of daos objects

summary: Swap out the use of rdb_tx_fetch with rdb_tx_iterate
description: The snapshot feature uses the rdb_tx_fetch method for finding snapshots immediately preceding and following a deleted snapshot. When RDB is moved from DBTree to VOS as its underlying implementation, the LE (less than or equal) and GE (greater than equal) operators are unsupported in its current state. Including support for the search feature is a non-trivial amount of effort, in which case, the only other alternative (and less complicated approach) is using rdb_tx_iterate to perform a manual search.
